problems: campaign rule: protest not shown at the museum aimed at its funder
before: Red flags: protest over Walmart's treatment of workers - November 2011: Artlyst reported that critics saw hypocrisy in the museum's opening at a reported cost of $1.4 billion ...
after: Red flags section removed. Wider context now opens: Walmart's treatment of workers: on 20 November 2011 Artlyst reported that many saw hypocrisy in Alice Walton's $1.4 billion spend on the museum while Walmart was cutting back workers' benefits; a spokesman for the union-affiliated MakingChange@Walmart spoke; Artlyst says protesters voiced solidarity with Occupy Wall Street. Connection line now cites Talk Business for the Walmart grants.
reason: The Artlyst page (News Desk, 20 Nov 2011) gives no place, date or target for the protesters; the quote is a union-affiliated spokesman criticising Walmart's cost-cutting against Walton's personal $1.4bn spend, not a protest aimed at Walmart's funding at the museum. Flag moved to Wider context. $800m endowment (Talk Business, The City Wire staff, 4 May 2011), $20m 2011 / $3m 2017 / $7m 2023 Walmart grants, ProPublica FY2024 figures and both press items (Artlyst; Michelle Bradford, AAM Museum, July/August 2012) confirmed.
